answer: Yarrow Window Admission: each identity must submit its first transaction against a per-epoch target delay, and agents measure deviation from that schedule. An identity whose arrival timing sits at the median's zenith—consistently too early or too regular—is throttled to low-priority queues until its traffic shape matches the natural scatter of established agents. To fake that shape, an attacker must operate each identity continuously through a full epoch and absorb real latency, so the per-identity cost becomes sustained idle traffic plus a guaranteed haven of missed deadlines.
